\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ചരക്ക്} (carakkŭ)}{ചരക്ക് (carakkŭ)}]{\ml{ചരക്ക്} (carakkŭ) — goods; cargo}

\label{lesson:ML-C467-carakku}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a cloakroom, then the Malayalam for to drag along.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ചരക്ക്}}
\textbf{\ml{ചരക്ക്}} — \emph{carakkŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}goods; cargo\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{തുറമുഖത്ത്} \ml{ധാരാളം} \ml{ചരക്ക്} \ml{ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tuṟamukhattŭ dhārāḷaṁ carakkŭ uṇṭāyirunnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a lot of cargo at the port.
\end{quote}

You met it inside \ml{പലചരക്ക്}, groceries: many goods.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ചരക്ക്}} (\emph{carakkŭ}) is native Dravidian, \textquotedblleft{}merchandise, cargo\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 2353). The same word sits inside \ml{പലചരക്ക്}, groceries.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{carakkŭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{carakkŭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuṟamukhattŭ dhārāḷaṁ carakkŭ uṇṭāyirunnu.} — There was a lot of cargo at the port.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a cloakroom, then the Malayalam for to drag along, then say \emph{carakkŭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ചരക്ക്} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Goods; cargo\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ലോറി} (lōṟi)}{ലോറി (lōṟi)}]{\ml{ലോറി} (lōṟi) — a lorry}

\label{lesson:ML-C467-lori}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to drag along, then the Malayalam for goods.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ലോറി}}
\textbf{\ml{ലോറി}} — \emph{lōṟi} — \textquotedblleft{}a lorry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഒരു} \ml{വലിയ} \ml{ലോറി} \ml{പാലത്തിന്} \ml{മുകളിലൂടെ} \ml{പോയി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{oru valiya lōṟi pālattinŭ mukaḷilūṭe pōyi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A big lorry went over the bridge.
\end{quote}

Malayalam keeps the British word; a truck is a \ml{ലോറി} too.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ലോറി}} (\emph{lōṟi}) was borrowed from English \emph{lorry}, a large goods vehicle.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lōṟi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lōṟi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oru valiya lōṟi pālattinŭ mukaḷilūṭe pōyi.} — A big lorry went over the bridge.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to drag along, then the Malayalam for goods, then say \emph{lōṟi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ലോറി} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A lorry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കയറ്റുക} (kayaṟṟuka)}{കയറ്റുക (kayaṟṟuka)}]{\ml{കയറ്റുക} (kayaṟṟuka) — to put on board; to load}

\label{lesson:ML-C467-kayarruka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for goods, then the Malayalam for a lorry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കയറ്റുക}}
\textbf{\ml{കയറ്റുക}} — \emph{kayaṟṟuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to put on board; to load\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{തൊഴിലാളികൾ} \ml{ചാക്കുകൾ} \ml{ലോറിയിൽ} \ml{കയറ്റി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{toḻilāḷikaḷ cākkukaḷ lōṟiyil kayaṟṟi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The workers loaded the sacks onto the lorry.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{കയറ്റി}, \emph{kayaṟṟi}.

The causative of \ml{കയറുക}, to climb in: you climb in, but you load a thing. The place takes -\ml{ഇൽ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കയറ്റുക}} (\emph{kayaṟṟuka}) is native Dravidian, the causative of \ml{കയറുക}, to climb or embark (DEDR 1255).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kayaṟṟuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kayaṟṟuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{toḻilāḷikaḷ cākkukaḷ lōṟiyil kayaṟṟi.} — The workers loaded the sacks onto the lorry.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for goods, then the Malayalam for a lorry, then say \emph{kayaṟṟuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കയറ്റുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To put on board; to load\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഇറക്കുക} (iṟakkuka)}{ഇറക്കുക (iṟakkuka)}]{\ml{ഇറക്കുക} (iṟakkuka) — to unload; to bring down}

\label{lesson:ML-C467-irakkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a lorry, then the Malayalam for to put on board.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഇറക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ഇറക്കുക}} — \emph{iṟakkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to unload; to bring down\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അവർ} \ml{ലോറിയിൽ} \ml{നിന്ന്} \ml{ചരക്ക്} \ml{ഇറക്കി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avar lōṟiyil ninnŭ carakkŭ iṟakki.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They unloaded the goods from the lorry.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ഇറക്കി}, \emph{iṟakki}.

The causative of \ml{ഇറങ്ങുക}, to get down, a pair like \ml{കയറുക} and \ml{കയറ്റുക}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഇറക്കുക}} (\emph{iṟakkuka}) is native Dravidian, the causative of \ml{ഇറങ്ങുക}, to go down (DEDR 516).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṟakkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṟakkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avar lōṟiyil ninnŭ carakkŭ iṟakki.} — They unloaded the goods from the lorry.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a lorry, then the Malayalam for to put on board, then say \emph{iṟakkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഇറക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To unload; to bring down\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{പാക്ക്} \ml{ചെയ്യുക} (pākkŭ ceyyuka)}{പാക്ക് ചെയ്യുക (pākkŭ ceyyuka)}]{\ml{പാക്ക്} \ml{ചെയ്യുക} (pākkŭ ceyyuka) — to pack}

\label{lesson:ML-C467-pakku-ceyyuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to put on board, then the Malayalam for to unload.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{പാക്ക്} \ml{ചെയ്യുക}}
\textbf{\ml{പാക്ക്} \ml{ചെയ്യുക}} — \emph{pākkŭ ceyyuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to pack\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{യാത്രയുടെ} \ml{തലേന്ന്} \ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{ബാഗ്} \ml{പാക്ക്} \ml{ചെയ്തു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yātrayuṭe talēnnŭ ñān bāgŭ pākkŭ ceytu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I packed my bag the day before the journey.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{പാക്ക്} \ml{ചെയ്തു}, \emph{pākkŭ ceytu}.

Another English verb with \ml{ചെയ്യുക}. A packet is a \ml{പാക്കറ്റ്}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{പാക്ക്} \ml{ചെയ്യുക}} (\emph{pākkŭ ceyyuka}) is a Malayalam verb phrase built from \emph{pack}, which was borrowed from English, and the native verb \ml{ചെയ്യുക}, to do.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pākkŭ ceyyuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pākkŭ ceyyuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yātrayuṭe talēnnŭ ñān bāgŭ pākkŭ ceytu.} — I packed my bag the day before the journey.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to put on board, then the Malayalam for to unload, then say \emph{pākkŭ ceyyuka} again
\end{itemize}
